text:
raj: Heads up — planning schema deploy + paginated backfill for user_histories tonight 02:00 UTC. Adds `new_flag` bool (nullable) and index. Backfill ~12M rows via job. Want to avoid table locks. /cc @emma @sasha

deploy-bot: deploy scheduled by raj for 2026-03-22 02:00 UTC. Pipeline: schema-change -> canary -> rollout. Change window: 2 hours. Release notes: add nullable column + index + backfill job.

emma: Question — how are we creating the index? CONCURRENTLY?

sasha: Yes, plan is Postgres `CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY`. Also add column as nullable with no default to avoid rewrite. Backfill in batches. If using a numeric id cursor we can do `WHERE id > $last_id ORDER BY id LIMIT 10000` loop.

emma: Pasting proposed steps:
```
ALTER TABLE user_histories ADD COLUMN new_flag boolean;
-- create index without blocking writes
CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY idx_user_histories_new_flag ON user_histories(new_flag);
-- backfill job (pseudo)
FOR batch IN batches:
  UPDATE user_histories SET new_flag = true WHERE id IN (SELECT id FROM user_histories WHERE new_flag IS NULL ORDER BY id LIMIT 10000);
```

mike: I'll own canary and metrics. Plan to pin web-service to v1.12.3 (no reads of new_flag) until backfill done, then roll to v1.13 that reads it. Also will enable feature flag after verifying correctness.

sasha: Important: CONCURRENTLY will fail if there are long-running txns — pre-flight: run `SELECT pid, age(now(), query_start), query FROM pg_stat_activity WHERE state = 'active' AND datname='prod' ORDER BY query_start DESC LIMIT 10;` and kill if >5m.

emma: Agreed. Also take logical backup and a snapshot before schema change. Add guardrails: abort if replication lag > 100MB or write QPS spike > 2x baseline.

raj: Rollback plan: schema changes are additive. If backfill causes issues we can pause job and flip feature flag to stop reads. For the index/column: to remove would require a drop column later; aim to avoid rollback unless data-corruption. So plan: feature flag first fallback, then stop job, then DB restore as last resort.

mike: On-call runbook notes: if error logs show >1% 500s in canary within 10m -> immediate rollback to service pin + kill backfill + alert DB infra.

deploy-bot: Starting schema change pipeline (job id: 93741). Will post status updates.

sasha: Quick housekeeping — set maintenance page and announce to #support 10m before.

emma: 👍 I'll run the preflight checks 30m before. mike — can you own monitoring dashboard and set alert thresholds?

mike: ✅ on it. I'll post the dashboard link in 15m.

deploy-bot: schema change pipeline succeeded: step 1 ADD COLUMN done. Backfill job started (job id: bj-2026-03-22-02-16). Monitoring: initial batch processed 10k rows in 4s.

mike: Canary looks clean for 10m. latency stable. No errors.

sasha: Backfill throughput looks fine. Still watching for long txns.

deploy-bot: Alert: migration job bj-2026-03-22-02:45 encountered deadlock on shard 4. Job paused automatically. Reason: long transaction holding row-level lock.

emma: Pause confirmed. Flipping feature flag off for canary traffic.

mike: Rolling service back to v1.12.3 for canary. Notifying infra to kill offending txns.

sasha: After killing the txns we should resume the job with smaller batch size (5k) and add index throttling.

raj: Good call. Update the runbook: if deadlocks -> pause, kill txns, reduce batch to 5k, resume. Keep feature flag off until 50% of rows processed.

deploy-bot: Backfill job resumed with batch size=5k. Monitoring continues.

mike: Canary re-enabled. Watching SLOs.

sasha: Note for postmortem: consider switching to async worker using logical decoding for next time to avoid row-level contention.

raj: Thanks everyone. Will write release notes and add postmortem if we hit incident threshold. Closing thread when backfill completes.
